verdict.reasoning: Doctor opens with, “You said you're a bit short of breath, is that right?” and patient replies “Yeah, yeah. Feeling very sort of breathless recently,” confirming shortness of breath.
Patient states, “whenever I like. Breathe deeply, it sort of catches in the right hand side of my back,” indicating right-sided back pain with deep breathing.

Duration: Doctor asks, “how long has this been going on for now?” Patient: “Just. Just a day, really.” Symptoms: she reports breathlessness and that it “catches in the right hand side of my back” with deep breathing.
Patient says, “I coughed up a bit of blood on two occasions,” and the doctor summarizes, “in the last day or so, that's when you get the cough and the pain inside and you've coughed blood.”
Patient reports, “I've had. I've got a bit of a slight fever,” matching the claim of slight fever.
Patient states, “I sort of feel my heart beating,” and doctor clarifies, “you can feel your heart kind of beating a bit faster, you think, than normal?” indicating palpitations.

Patient: “I've been feeling a bit like a bit tired at work... performing daily activities has been a bit harder than usual.” Duration: Doctor asks, “how long has that been for the tiredness...?” Patient: “Only for a couple of weeks or so.”

Patient says, “exercising has been a bit difficult because I've been feeling tired,” and confirms this has been “for a couple of weeks or so,” indicating reduced exercise tolerance for about two weeks.
When asked why she is on methotrexate, patient says, “I've got sle,” i.e., systemic lupus erythematosus.
Patient confirms regular medication: “Yeah. Methotrexate. Methotrexate.” and later, “This morning,” when asked when she last took it.
Doctor: “Do you have any allergies to any medication?” Patient: “No.” Doctor: “Any other allergies at all?” Patient: “No.” Also later: “Do you have any allergies to any antibiotics?” Patient: “No.”
Doctor asks, “do you smoke at all?” Patient responds, “No.”
Patient answers occupation: “I work in an office. Just a desk job.”
Doctor: “And do you live alone?” Patient: “Yes.” Doctor: “In a flat or a house?” Patient: “Flat.”
Doctor: “Do you have any pets?” Patient: “Cats?” Doctor: “A cat. Okay.” indicating a cat as pet.
After counting pulse, doctor concludes, “that was about 11 or 12. So that would make your heart rate about 66 to 74. That's okay.”
After the capillary refill maneuver, doctor says, “Okay, perfect. That's great. Thank you so much,” implying no abnormality noted.

Doctor performs throat view (“If you position your device… say ah.” “Perfect. Thank you for that. Excellent.”) but does not explicitly state that the examination was normal or that there were no abnormalities.
Doctor asks patient to feel neck glands; patient: “No, they feel pretty normal to me.” This supports absence of palpable lymphadenopathy.
Doctor states: “what I think we need to do is this sounds like you might have a chest infection.”

Doctor links symptoms: “if you've got this kind of pain when taking a deep breath in and you're coughing up blood, we do need to assess you to figure out whether you have a pneumonia or chest infection,” and references fever earlier, supporting SOB/pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, and fever as relevant symptoms.

Doctor says, “we do need to assess you to figure out whether you have a pneumonia or chest infection,” and later discusses excluding lung cancer and possible need for chest X‑ray, indicating pneumonia vs. other lung pathology as differential considerations.
Doctor: “What I think we'll do is we'll arrange for you to get reviewed in a clinic today.”
Doctor: “someone needs to listen to your chest and maybe check your blood pressure as well,” specifying chest auscultation.
Same sentence: “listen to your chest and maybe check your blood pressure as well and check that you're stable... and to recheck your pulse as well.”
Doctor includes, “Check your temperature, make sure all those parameters are okay,” as part of in-person review.

Doctor: “You may well need an antibiotic… I'm not going to prescribe anything for you now because I think you need to have that basic assessment first before we proceed to the next step. But that's what I would predict the next step might be,” indicating conditional antibiotic therapy.

Doctor discusses lung cancer and investigations: “we might need to get some investigations to exclude that… we may end up having to do a follow up chest X ray if things don't settle down,” implying future discussion of differential and imaging if symptoms persist.

Doctor: “I'm going to leave the number in the notes for this appointment for you to ring our support team and then they will book you in for a face to face appointment,” providing contact information to arrange the clinic appointment.
